cards.explanation: The answer is True. Peter says they have “…received a faith as precious as ours…” He doesn't put their faith on a lower shelf. He sets it right beside his own. I think that's a mighty kind way to open a letter. (2 Peter 1:1)

The answer is the knowledge of God and of Jesus. Peter writes, “Grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.” That's the wish he opens his letter with. Multiplied, friends. That's a big word to start with, and knowing God and Jesus is how he says it happens. (2 Peter 1:2)

The answer is everything we need. Peter says, “His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness…” Everything, friends. That's the whole kitchen, not a starter kit. Notice it says “has given,” so it's already in our hands. (2 Peter 1:3)

The answer is so they can share in God's own nature. Peter says the promises were given “…so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature…” That's the reason he names. Think about how big that is, friends. Someone who once sat in a junk drawer is still getting his head around it. (2 Peter 1:4)

The answer is False. Peter says they've already escaped. His words are “…now that you have escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.” Nobody's standing in line for it. It's behind them, friends. (2 Peter 1:4)

The answer is faith. Peter says, “…make every effort to add to your faith virtue…” Faith is what they already have, and everything else gets added to it. Faith is the dough, friends, and the toppings come after. (2 Peter 1:5)

The answer is False. Peter keeps adding after virtue. Right behind it he writes “and to virtue, knowledge…” and the list keeps going all the way to love. Virtue is where the list begins, not where it ends. (2 Peter 1:5-7)

The answer is on top of the one before it. Each quality gets added to the last one. Peter writes “…and to knowledge, self-control…” and keeps going the same way. Nothing in the list gets swapped out. They stack, friends. (2 Peter 1:5-7)

The answer is True. Peter says that if you possess these qualities and continue to grow in them, “…they will keep you from being ineffective and unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Notice the two parts of his if: having the qualities, and continuing to grow in them. Ineffective and unproductive are the two things he says they keep you from. I'm still working on the growing part myself, friends. (2 Peter 1:8)

The answer is that he was cleansed from his past sins. Peter says this person has “…forgotten that he has been cleansed from his past sins.” That's the thing he's lost sight of. The cleansing already happened, friends, and he's forgotten it. (2 Peter 1:9)

The answer is they will never stumble. Peter writes, “For if you practice these things you will never stumble…” Never, friends. I trip over my own mustache on a good day, so I like hearing that word. The if in his sentence is practicing these things. (2 Peter 1:10)

The answer is a lavish reception. Peter writes, “…you will receive a lavish reception into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.” Lavish, friends. That's no sticker and a handshake at the door. He says it's waiting in the eternal kingdom of Jesus, and that's worth keeping the ovens ready for. (2 Peter 1:11)
